key_concepts: Earth's surface is about 71% water and 29% land.
Earth's crust is the thin, outermost solid layer of the planet.
Continental crust is thicker, less dense, and made mostly of granitic rocks.
Oceanic crust is thinner, denser, and made mostly of basaltic rocks.
Oceanic crust is continually created and destroyed by seafloor spreading and subduction.
Lithospheric plates are large solid regions made of the crust and uppermost mantle.
Plates float on the semi-fluid asthenosphere and move due to mantle convection currents.
Major plates include the Pacific, Eurasian, African, and Philippine Sea plates.
Divergent boundaries create new crust through seafloor spreading.
Convergent boundaries form mountain ranges and volcanic arcs through subduction.
Transform boundaries cause earthquakes as plates slide horizontally past each other.
Plate tectonics explains the distribution of continents, oceans, volcanoes, and earthquake
